raw.rationale: Phenformin is a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor whose cytotoxicity at 2.5 µM over 5 days is largely driven by organic cation transporter (OCT1/SLC22A1) expression and reliance on oxidative phosphorylation, making selective killing most plausible in liver cancer (high OCT1) and possibly lung/colorectal subsets, while most lineages show little selective effect. Published PRISM-type screens generally show phenformin as weakly selective, with the strongest signals in liver and occasional metabolic-dependency lineages.
